_comment: Modern felt-consequence 'stakes' dealt per chapter by src/librarian/stakesPlan.ts. Reader feedback: chapters are 'more useful than exciting' — keys/bills/drawers are practical, not gripping. These are broad, modern, everyday costs a wide/younger reader feels in the body, dealt as a per-chapter MENU (the writer lands one that fits in an example or the framing; an ill-fitting stake is never forced). 13 entries (prime — required by the stakesPlan step math); each is a CONTENT cue ('name the cost'), never a scene position.

stakes.definition: money that isn't there when it's due — rent you can't cover, a payment that bounces, an account overdrawn at the worst moment
the device that fails right when it matters — phone at 1% before a trip, charger gone before work, no signal during the call you needed
the opening that slips away — a job lead, intro, or referral missed or buried until it's gone
the one message that mattered, lost in a flooded group chat or a wall of notifications, answered too late or not at all
the deadline missed because the work scattered — a form, a submission, an assignment due that quietly slid past
a health-or-people cost you forgot — a missed dose, a skipped appointment, the person you meant to check on and didn't
the reply you meant to send and never did, and the relationship that cools because of it
money draining quietly — a subscription you forgot, a late fee, a renewal you'd have cancelled if you'd seen it
two commitments at once — the thing you have to drop, the person you let down, the trust that takes the hit
the thing gone the moment you need it — keys, ID, AirPods, the one file, the note you swore you saved
the slow cost of an overloaded mind — tired, scattered, ten things half-done and nothing finished, the day gone with nothing to show
looking scattered when it counts — walking into the meeting, class, or conversation without the one thing you needed
the moment that doesn't come back — the event missed, the chance to say it gone, the deadline for the good version passed
